title: A uniform exponent saving for arbitrary generalized convolution
formal: Does there exist an absolute \(\varepsilon >0\) such that, for every fixed finite domain D with \(d=|D|\ge 2\) and every fixed function \(f:D\times D\to D\), the entire f-convolution of two integer tables on \(D^{n}\) can be computed exactly in \(\widetilde{O}\)\((d^{(2- \varepsilon )n}\cdot \operatorname{polylog}(2+M))\) time? The same \(\varepsilon\) must work for all domains and operations; n is unbounded and M bounds the absolute input values. No associativity, commutativity or algebraic structure of f is assumed.
context:
Many exact algorithms combine two tables of partial solutions coordinate by coordinate. The function f specifies how one pair of coordinate states combines; the convolution sums the contributions of every compatible pair.

There are \(d^{n}\) entries in each input table and in the output, whereas there are \(d^{2n}\) pairs of input indices. The question asks for a fixed saving in this exponent for arbitrary coordinate-combination rules.

The journal theorem computes the full convolution in \(\widetilde{O}\)\((((3/4)d^{2})^{n} \operatorname{polylog} M)\) for even d; for odd d the base is \((3/4)d^{2}+(1/4)d\). This improves the conference constant \(5/6\).

For even d the known bound corresponds to \(\varepsilon _{d}=\log _{d}(4/3)\). It is positive for each fixed d but approaches zero as d grows. The open question requires a single positive \(\varepsilon\) valid for all d.

The paper also obtains \(\widetilde{O}\)\((d^{\omega n/2} \operatorname{polylog} M)\) for one requested output entry, where \(\omega\) is the matrix-multiplication exponent. The card requires all \(d^{n}\) entries within the total time bound.
why: Would give a broadly applicable improvement for table-merging computations without requiring an algebraic law on the state-combination operation, strengthening a common primitive in exact and parameterized algorithms.
status_note: Read the IPEC question and the improved Algorithmica version, including its retained Section 6 question. Checked the January 2023 arXiv revision and later exact-title/generalized-convolution searches through 12 September 2026; no result meeting the uniform exponent target was found.

progress.text: The conference paper beats brute force by a factor \((6/5)^{n}\) for even d and asks for an absolute saving in the d-exponent.
The revised preprint improves the constant to \(3/4\); the Algorithmica version retains the absolute-exponent-saving question.

importance.reason: A general exact-computation primitive whose improvements can transfer across many dynamic programs, rather than a speedup for one chosen operation. Existing score retained.

sentences: Generalized convolution combines two integer tables using an arbitrary operation on each coordinate.
The card asks to compute the entire output table with a fixed saving over the brute-force exponent.
The saving must be independent of the size of the coordinate domain.
The improved journal algorithm reduces the exponential base by a constant factor, which gives a domain-dependent exponent saving only.
A faster algorithm for one output entry does not meet the full-table target.

definitions: Identify D with \(\{0,\ldots ,d- 1\}\). For \(u,w\in D^{n}\) set \((u\oplus _{f} w)_{j}=f(u_{j},w_{j})\) for \(1\le j\le n\). Input tables \(g,h:D^{n}\to \{- M,\ldots ,M\}\), with \(n\ge 1\) and \(M\ge 1\), list every signed integer in binary. The output is the full table \(C:D^{n}\to Z\), where \(C(v)=\sum_{u,w\in D^{n}: u\oplus _{f} w=v}g(u)h(w)\); an empty sum is zero. All arithmetic is ordinary integer arithmetic. In the source’s fixed-operation convention, D and the finite \(d^{2}\)-entry table of f specify the convolution problem; the growing inputs are g,h. More explicitly, the requested bound means a deterministic algorithm, uniform in n and the input tables, taking at most \(C_{D,f} d^{(2- \varepsilon )n}(1+n \log  d+\log (2+M))^{a_{D,f}}\) bit operations, for constants \(C_{D,f},a_{D,f}\) depending only on D,f. Any finite preparation of that fixed table can be included in \(C_{D,f}; \varepsilon\) is chosen before D,f. This states the fixed-domain asymptotic question from the source, not a bound for reading an arbitrary operation table when \(n=1\). Standard random-access storage of the listed tables is permitted, with arithmetic charged for operand bit length; addressing costs are absorbed in the displayed polynomial factor. Each output has \(O(n \log  d+\log (2+M))\) bits. The target concerns every output entry, not a query for a single specified v.
answer_criterion: Establish the bound with one positive \(\varepsilon\) independent of D and f, for all fixed finite operations and all input tables, or refute that universally quantified existence claim in the stated deterministic exact-computation model. An exponent saving that tends to zero with d, a theorem restricted to selected operations, or a faster single-entry query algorithm does not suffice.
